lessons.claim: Keep a baseline as a control while probing different mechanisms and budget-scaling methods.
lessons.scope: Research portfolios with an executable baseline and bounded budget
lessons.limitations: Long-run scalability is not fixed-budget superiority; implementation checks remain necessary.
lessons.falsification: Review portfolio breadth if matched-budget forward comparisons repeatedly yield fewer useful discoveries or worse selections than focused search; one failed probe does not refute the principle.

lessons.claim: Validation must represent the generalization target and preserve sample dependence.
lessons.scope: Prediction and agent evaluation; sampling units are task-dependent
lessons.limitations: Local splits may miss future shift; repeated folds are dependent.
lessons.falsification: Frozen local rankings fail prospective outcomes; audit distribution, leakage and estimators.

lessons.claim: Responsive opponent populations may reveal weaknesses hidden by latest-champion testing.
lessons.scope: Adversarial games with possible nontransitivity and versioned policies
lessons.limitations: Finite pools and approximate best responses cannot prove global robustness or equilibrium.
lessons.falsification: Reconsider the population design if equal-budget prospective comparisons do not improve weakness discovery or selection quality versus champion-only evaluation; an exploitable candidate alone is not a refutation.

lessons.claim: Plan, learn and execute with legal information and explicit horizon/resource assumptions.
lessons.scope: Sequential competitions with simulator or trajectory access
lessons.limitations: Known transitions do not imply observable hidden state; shaping and truncation can alter preferences.
lessons.falsification: Observation-only closed-loop or longer-horizon evaluation overturns apparent benefit.

lessons.claim: Versioned literature-and-experiment memory may improve competition research decisions.
lessons.scope: Research assistance, not underlying weights or guaranteed score gains
lessons.limitations: Prompt tests alone do not establish competition-performance improvement.
lessons.falsification: Forward tasks or measured competitions show no improvement or harmful rigidity.
